From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: Candidate models, TPS/p99 snapshot & perf dossier

Hi Ellie / Mark —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and the artifacts I promised:

What we heard
- Primary goal: extract structured data from user-submitted documents (OCR outputs + chat summaries) with strict p99 latency targets for interactive UI slices (~500ms).
- Expected throughput for initial pilot: 120 concurrent users, ~60 requests/sec peak.
- Data sensitivity: PHI touches; you need private deployment or VPC + KMS for keys.

Model shortlist (Redwood-verified) — recommended starting slate
1) rwd-3b-curie-opt (8-bit quantized): best latency/cost tradeoff for single-turn extraction.
   - Typical TPS: 280 requests/sec on a 8xA10 pool (batched), p50 45ms, p95 110ms, p99 340ms for 512B seq.
2) rwd-7b-guard (mixed-kernel): higher quality on long-form context, TPS ~90, p50 95ms, p95 210ms, p99 460ms.
3) rwd-13b-quant (8-bit, KV cache enabled): fallback for edge cases, TPS ~45, p50 160ms, p95 350ms, p99 820ms.

Artifacts attached/shared
- redwood_perf_profiles_quanta.pdf (concise profile per model: throughput, p50/p95/p99, memory footprint) — attached.
- quantaforce_benchmarks.csv (raw run results from our sandbox using your sample prompts) — attached.
- qf_prompt_set_v1.zip (sanitized prompt set we used for benching) — attached.
- Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/0B1QF-QuantaForce-perf-dossier

Quality/regression notes
- We observed occasional hallucination on long nested lists with rwd-3b-curie-opt; mitigation is to add stricter output schema enforcement + token-level post-filtering.
- We recommend a regression guardrail: run continuous evals on your golden prompts (we can host the evals or provide CI hooks).

Next steps (suggested)
1) Confirm privacy/deployment preference (Hosted w/ dedicated tenant vs Dedicated vs Private VPC).
2) Approve a two-week micro-pilot: Redwood runs a focused benchmark on your sanitized dataset (we provision 2xA10 dedicated for parity).
3) Procurement: if pilot looks good, we’ll draft a scoped pilot SOW and pilot pricing.

If you’d like I can run a short re-benchmark constrained to the exact prompt workflows you use — that will give a tighter p99 estimate.

Cheers,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.ai
Attachment: redwood_perf_profiles_quanta.pdf (3 pages), quantaforce_benchmarks.csv (CSV, 120KB), qf_prompt_set_v1.zip (ZIP, 45KB)

Ellie — quick answers and a condensed snapshot below. Attached is the one-page table you asked for (also uploaded to Drive).

Short answers
- Condensed TPS/p99 table: attached (redwood_perf_profiles_quanta.pdf, page 1). We ran benches at 256/512/1024 tokens; numbers below are from the 512B column for quick reference.
- Private VPC: yes, we support customer-managed KMS and can integrate your HSM for key wrapping. KV cache retention is configurable per-deployment (default 72 hours; can be set to 0 for strict no-cache).
- Pilot SOW: I’ve uploaded a pilot_sow_template.docx to the same Drive folder and will share a ballpark: $12k for the two-week dedicated micro-pilot (includes reserved 2xA10, engineering support, and eval reports). Final SOW depends on runhours and data-sensitivity add-ons.

Condensed snapshot (512B, single-request latency profile; numbers are medians across 10 runs)
- rwd-3b-curie-opt: TPS=280; p50=45ms; p95=110ms; p99=340ms
- rwd-7b-guard: TPS=90; p50=95ms; p95=210ms; p99=460ms
- rwd-13b-quant: TPS=45; p50=160ms; p95=350ms; p99=820ms

Regression guardrails we propose
- Continuous evals: run your golden prompts daily, alert on any >5% accuracy drop.
- Canary routing: serve 95% traffic on primary model with 5% routed to higher-quality variant for sampling.
- Fallback policy: on p99 violation we can auto-route to a higher-capacity instance (cost tradeoff documented in the perf dossier).

Telemetry needs for the micro-bench
- Sample prompts (sanitized) — you provided a good set; if you can add 200 more edge-case prompts that’d be ideal.
- Expected concurrency profile (minute-level) for peak 30 minutes during day.
- Any disallowed token patterns (PII/PHI redaction rules).

Next steps
- I’ll 1) post the one-pager, 2) copy a pilot SOW template, and 3) queue an engineer to run the focused micro-bench once we get your OK and sample prompts.

Would it help if we scheduled a short (30m) pilot kickoff tomorrow to align on data handoff and VPC details?

Best,
Rafael
Attachment: redwood_perf_profiles_quanta.pdf (one-page summary), pilot_sow_template.docx (DOCX)
